source_meta._title: Some NBT tags require the correct suffix

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.11.2 in single-player on the integrated server. Use a fresh Creative-mode world with cheats enabled, difficulty set to Easy, nighttime, and the default mobGriefing=true gamerule. A Superflat world is selected as a practical convenience so the target zombie and dropped item are easy to see. Default keyboard and mouse controls are assumed.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft Java Edition 1.11.2, the first version listed as affected.
Use a fresh world so that unrelated entities and changed gamerules do not interfere with the test.
Cheats must be enabled because the report's reproduction uses the /summon command.
Difficulty must not be Peaceful, because the summoned zombie must remain present.
Leave the mobGriefing gamerule at its fresh-world default value of true.
Perform the test at night so the zombie does not ignite in direct sunlight.
Do not add the byte suffix b to the CanPickUpLoot value in the target summon command; the target command must contain exactly CanPickUpLoot:1.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation that uses release 1.11.2, start it, and verify that the title screen identifies the running version as Minecraft 1.11.2.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft 1.11.2 main menu is displayed.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then select Create New World to open the world-creation screen.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Set Game Mode to Creative. Open More World Options, set Allow Cheats to ON, and cycle World Type to Superflat. Return to the main world-creation screen after configuring those options.
steps.success_cue: The new world is configured for Creative mode with cheats enabled and the Superflat world type selected.

steps.action: Select Create New World. After the world opens, wait until the terrain has rendered and movement and inventory input respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally in a fully loaded Creative-mode world.

steps.action: Set the difficulty to Easy so the zombie will not be removed as it would be on Peaceful. Press T to open chat, enter the command exactly as shown including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the difficulty was changed to Easy.

steps.action: Prevent the target zombie from burning in daylight. Press T, enter the command exactly as shown including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The world is visibly at night and the sky is dark.

steps.action: Obtain one Diamond Sword as a clear equippable test item. Press E to open the Creative inventory, open the Search Items tab identified by the compass icon, search for Diamond Sword, and click or drag a Diamond Sword into an empty hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine slots along the bottom of the inventory. Close the inventory with E or Esc.
steps.success_cue: A Diamond Sword is present in one of the nine hotbar slots and the inventory screen is closed.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Diamond Sword by pressing that slot's number key, 1 through 9, or by scrolling the mouse wheel until the slot is highlighted.
steps.exact_input: 1-9 corresponding to the Diamond Sword hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: The Diamond Sword's hotbar slot is highlighted and the sword is visible in the player's hand.

steps.action: Summon the target zombie using the report's command. Press T to open chat, type the command exactly as shown including the leading slash, and press Enter. Preserve the capitalization of CanPickUpLoot and use the unsuffixed value 1; do not change it to 1b.
steps.success_cue: One zombie appears at or immediately adjacent to the player's current position, and the submitted command contains CanPickUpLoot:1 rather than CanPickUpLoot:1b.

steps.action: Use the movement controls, normally W, A, S, and D, to separate from the newly summoned zombie without attacking it. Keep the Diamond Sword selected and position the player approximately one to two blocks from that specific zombie.
steps.success_cue: The target zombie is alive, clearly visible, and approximately one to two blocks in front of the player.

steps.action: Aim toward the target zombie's lower body or feet so that an item dropped forward from the player's active slot will land immediately beside the zombie rather than several blocks away.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair is aimed at the ground or lower body directly beside the target zombie, with no wall or obstacle between the player and zombie.

steps.action: Press the Drop Selected Item control once—Q by default—to throw the selected Diamond Sword toward the target zombie. Do not press Q repeatedly, attack the zombie, enter another command, or summon a replacement zombie after this action.
steps.success_cue: The Diamond Sword has left the player's hotbar and has been thrown to a landing point within immediate item-pickup range of the zombie summoned with CanPickUpLoot:1.

stor.handoff_condition: The Diamond Sword has just been dropped within immediate pickup range of the living zombie summoned by /summon zombie ~ ~ ~ {CanPickUpLoot:1}. Begin observation now without providing additional player input or replacing the target zombie.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, seed, world type, difficulty, time of day, or test item. Creative mode, a fresh Superflat world, Easy difficulty, nighttime, and a Diamond Sword are practical choices intended to make the supplied reproduction deterministic without changing its NBT condition.
The report says only to throw an item at the zombie. A Diamond Sword is selected because it is visually distinct, cannot stack, and is an equippable item for a zombie with an empty main hand.

The command summons the zombie at the player's exact relative coordinates (~ ~ ~), so the zombie may initially overlap the player. The plan therefore includes moving a short distance away before dropping the item.

The suffixed CanPickUpLoot:1b command mentioned by the report is not executed in this primary reproduction path because the handoff must occur immediately after triggering the unsuffixed test case, before evaluating behavior.

source_meta._title: Survival tab of Creative inventory desyncs if changed manually after an external change

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 20w46a in a single-player world using the integrated server. Use Creative mode with commands enabled. Default controls are assumed: T for chat, E for inventory, Q for Drop Selected Item, number key 1 for Hotbar Slot 1, and right-click for Use Item/Place Block. No datapack or resource pack is required for the updated formal reproduction steps.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected version 20w46a rather than the fix version 24w33a.
Use a Creative-mode player that is not in Spectator mode.
Commands must be available for the deterministic inventory-clearing and item-acquisition steps; a newly created single-player Creative world normally satisfies this condition.
Use a flat, solid area with air above the ground and no nearby lava, fire, water currents, hoppers, or other players that could remove the dropped Stone item.
The player inventory, hotbar, armor slots, and offhand must be empty before obtaining the single Stone item.
Complete the drop-to-inventory-opening transition promptly so that the Survival Inventory tab is open before the dropped Stone is picked up.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using the historical installation for version 20w46a.
steps.success_cue: The title screen visibly identifies the running game version as 20w46a.

steps.action: Create a new single-player world with Game Mode set to Creative and commands/cheats enabled, or load an existing world that already provides those conditions.
steps.success_cue: The player is inside a world in Creative mode and can open chat commands.

steps.action: Wait for world loading to finish before manipulating the inventory.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered, player movement responds normally, and the player is standing rather than still viewing a loading screen.

steps.action: Move onto a flat, solid ground surface. Ensure there is room for a dropped item to remain near the player's feet and at least one exposed ground block nearby on which a block could normally be placed.
steps.exact_input: Use the bound movement controls; defaults are W, A, S, and D.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on solid ground in a clear area, with no hazard or collection mechanism next to the player's feet.

steps.action: Clear the player's inventory deterministically. Press T to open chat, enter the command exactly as shown including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The hotbar, main inventory, armor slots, and offhand contain no items. If any slot was not cleared, remove its contents before continuing.

steps.action: Give the player exactly one Stone item. Press T, enter the command exactly as shown including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Exactly one Stone item is present in the otherwise empty inventory; because the inventory was empty, it should occupy the first hotbar slot.

steps.action: Select the first hotbar slot using the Hotbar Slot 1 control.
steps.success_cue: The first hotbar slot is highlighted, it contains exactly one Stone, and the Stone is visible in the player's main hand.

steps.action: Prime the required Creative inventory tab before performing the timing-sensitive drop. Press E, locate the tab whose hover tooltip reads "Survival Inventory," and left-click that tab.
steps.exact_input: E, then left-click the tab labeled "Survival Inventory"
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory is open on the Survival Inventory tab, showing the player's armor slots, main inventory, and hotbar rather than a Creative item-category grid.

steps.action: Close the inventory while leaving the Survival Inventory tab selected so that it can be reopened quickly after dropping the item.
steps.success_cue: The world view is visible again, the first hotbar slot remains selected, and the single Stone remains in the player's main hand.

steps.action: Aim the camera nearly straight downward so that dropping the selected item sends it directly toward the solid ground at the player's feet.
steps.exact_input: Move the mouse until the crosshair points at the ground immediately below the player.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair is aimed at the ground at the player's feet and the selected Stone is still in hotbar slot 1.

steps.action: Drop the single selected Stone item once using the Drop Selected Item control. Do not hold the control or use the drop-stack modifier.
steps.success_cue: The first hotbar slot is visibly empty and a rotating Stone item entity is on the ground very close to the player's feet.

steps.action: Immediately reopen the Creative inventory before the dropped Stone is automatically picked up.
steps.success_cue: An inventory screen is open while the Stone item entity is still awaiting pickup or while its pickup is just being processed.

steps.action: Confirm that the open screen is the Survival Inventory tab. If another Creative tab opened, immediately left-click the tab whose hover tooltip reads "Survival Inventory." If the Stone was already picked up before this tab became active, clear the inventory and restart from the single-Stone setup.
steps.exact_input: If required, left-click the tab labeled "Survival Inventory".
steps.success_cue: The Survival Inventory tab is active before the pickup update is handled, and the player's hotbar and main inventory slots are visible and directly editable.

steps.action: Keep the Survival Inventory tab open and wait without moving the player or clicking an inventory slot until the player picks up the dropped Stone.
steps.success_cue: The ground item is collected and one Stone appears in the first hotbar slot while the Survival Inventory tab remains open.

steps.action: Without closing the inventory, manually move the newly collected Stone out of the first hotbar slot. Left-click the Stone in hotbar slot 1 to attach it to the cursor, then left-click the upper-left empty slot of the 3-by-9 main inventory grid to deposit it there.
steps.exact_input: Left-click hotbar slot 1, then left-click the upper-left slot of the main inventory grid.
steps.success_cue: The visible Stone is in the chosen main-inventory slot, hotbar slot 1 visibly contains no item, and the inventory screen has remained open throughout the move.

steps.action: Close the inventory after completing the manual slot move.
steps.success_cue: The world view is visible, the Stone is no longer shown in hotbar slot 1, and no inventory interface remains open.

steps.action: Explicitly select the first hotbar slot using the Hotbar Slot 1 control, even if it already appears selected.
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 1 is highlighted as the active main-hand slot, and the client visibly shows the main hand as empty.

steps.action: Aim at the exposed top face of a nearby solid ground block with empty air above it and enough distance that a newly placed block would not intersect the player's body. Press the Use Item/Place Block control exactly once.
steps.success_cue: The right-click use/place input has just been performed on a valid ground face while the visibly empty first hotbar slot is active.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just right-clicked once on a valid exposed ground face while hotbar slot 1 is active and visibly empty, after the externally picked-up Stone was manually moved to the main inventory without closing the Survival Inventory tab. Begin observation immediately after that input.
uncertainties: The report does not state that a dedicated server or multiple players are required. This plan uses single-player as the simplest environment preserving Creative-mode inventory synchronization behavior.

The report allows moving the collected Stone to any different hotbar or inventory slot but does not prescribe a specific destination. The upper-left slot of the main 3-by-9 inventory grid is selected as a deterministic destination.

The /clear and /give commands are execution conveniences and are not commands supplied by the report. They are used only to create the reported initial state of an otherwise empty inventory containing one Stone in the first hotbar slot.

The pickup timing can vary. If the Stone enters the inventory before the Survival Inventory tab is open, the attempt does not satisfy the reported ordering and must be restarted from the clear-inventory state.

The original description discusses an uploaded backpack datapack, but the later formal Steps to Reproduce describe a standalone Creative-inventory procedure. This plan follows those formal steps and does not install the datapack.
No external web verification was used because the report supplies the required affected versions and reproduction sequence, and the added operational details do not replace the report's instructions.

source_meta._title: Adding effects with an effects_changed advancement causes a packet error (ConcurrentModificationException) if it was triggered by Milk

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.21 in a fresh vanilla singleplayer world using the integrated server. Use Creative mode with commands/cheats enabled so the required item and initial status effect can be obtained deterministically. Install the supplied effect-bug-1.zip data pack before creating the world. Do not test in fix version 24w34a.
preconditions: Use the exact Java Edition release 1.21 listed as affected by the report.
Have the report attachment effect-bug-1.zip available as a local file.
Use a fresh world so the supplied advancement has no completion state left over from an earlier test.
Enable commands/cheats; Creative mode is selected only to simplify deterministic setup and is not stated as a bug requirement.
Keep effect-bug-1.zip enabled throughout the reproduction.
The player must have at least one active status effect immediately before drinking the milk.
Clear the effect specifically by finishing consumption of a milk bucket. Do not substitute /effect clear, because the report states that command clearing does not reproduce the issue.
No additional players are required. The report indicates the issue can occur in singleplayer through the integrated server as well as on a dedicated server.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an unmodified Java Edition installation for the exact release 1.21, launch it, and wait for the main menu.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left area of the main menu identifies the running version as Minecraft 1.21, with no snapshot or fix-version identifier such as 24w34a.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer, select Create New World, give the world any name, set Game Mode to Creative, and ensure commands/cheats are allowed. Creative mode and commands are setup conveniences rather than report-required gameplay conditions.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open for a new Creative world in which commands will be available.

steps.action: On the world-creation screen, open the More tab, select Data Packs, and select Open Pack Folder. Copy the supplied effect-bug-1.zip file into the folder that opens. Leave the archive as a .zip file; do not rename or reconstruct its contents.
steps.success_cue: After returning to Minecraft, an available data-pack entry corresponding to effect-bug-1.zip is visible on the Data Packs screen.

steps.action: Enable the effect-bug-1.zip entry by clicking its arrow so it moves from Available to Selected. Select Done, then select Create New World. If the file does not appear or cannot be enabled, stop rather than replacing it with a different data pack.
steps.success_cue: World creation begins with the effect-bug-1.zip entry in the selected/enabled data-pack list.

steps.action: Wait for the new world and integrated server to finish loading. Do not start the test while the loading screen is displayed.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the world, surrounding chunks are rendered, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Verify that the supplied data pack is enabled. Press T to open in-game chat, type the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat prints the enabled data-pack list and includes a file entry corresponding to effect-bug-1.zip. The command does not report an unknown-command, permission, or data-pack loading error.

steps.action: Obtain one milk bucket before applying the test effect. Press T, enter the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback states that a milk bucket was given, and a Milk Bucket is present in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: If the Milk Bucket is not already in one of the nine hotbar slots at the bottom of the screen, press E to open the inventory, move the Milk Bucket into any hotbar slot, and close the inventory with E or Esc.
steps.success_cue: A Milk Bucket icon is visible in one of the nine hotbar slots after the inventory is closed.

steps.action: Give the player a temporary, visible status effect. Press T, enter the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter. This uses Speed I for 120 seconds as the report permits any effect. Do not use /effect clear afterward.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback reports that Speed was applied to the player, and an active status-effect icon is visible.

steps.action: Confirm the milk precondition without clearing anything: press E to open the inventory, verify that at least one active status effect is listed, then close the inventory. Proceed promptly enough that the temporary Speed effect has not expired.
steps.success_cue: The inventory has been closed and the player still has at least one active status effect immediately before selecting the milk.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Milk Bucket by pressing its corresponding number key, 1 through 9, or by scrolling until that slot is outlined. Do not drink it yet.
steps.success_cue: The Milk Bucket is displayed in the player's hand and its hotbar slot has the active-slot outline.

steps.action: Drink the selected Milk Bucket: press and continuously hold the Use Item control, which is right mouse button by default, until the drinking animation finishes. Do not release the control early, switch slots, run /effect clear, or perform another action during consumption.
steps.exact_input: Hold right-click until milk consumption completes
steps.success_cue: The drinking animation has completed and the held Milk Bucket has become an empty Bucket. Immediately stop input and hand control to the observation subsystem.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just finished consuming the milk, the milk bucket has changed into an empty bucket, and no further command or player action has been performed. Begin observing the client connection and integrated-server state immediately.
uncertainties: The supplied report names effect-bug-1.zip but does not include the archive's internal files, namespace, advancement identifier, pack description, or any data-pack-generated confirmation message. The plan therefore verifies the attachment by its enabled file entry rather than by an unknown internal identifier.
The report does not require a particular game mode. Creative mode and commands are used only as a deterministic way to acquire milk and apply an initial effect.

The report states that the issue occurs in server handling and distinguishes singleplayer from non-singleplayer behavior, but it does not require a dedicated server. This plan chooses the simpler fresh singleplayer/integrated-server path.

The exact display label of the enabled data pack may differ from the attachment filename because a data pack can define its own description. The enabled entry must nevertheless correspond to effect-bug-1.zip.

External verification was used only for operational data-pack installation, reload/list behavior, Java /effect syntax, and milk's effect-clearing mechanic; it was not used to replace the report's reproduction sequence.
